title: mssql-mcp tool arguments can bypass SQL safety controls
summary: Unvalidated identifiers, predicates and stateFilter values are interpolated into SQL batches. Injection can execute during preview before confirmation and row-limit safeguards.

severity.rationale: Agent-controlled inputs can modify or disclose data outside the intended tool restrictions. Reader-tier injection also defeats assumptions about read-only tooling.

affected.note: Affected core <=0.5.0; server <=0.5.2; reader/writer <=0.4.2. Fixed core/server 0.6.0; reader/writer 0.5.0.

exposure: Attackers must influence MCP tool arguments. Database effects follow the configured login privileges; OS execution additionally requires privileged SQL configuration.

params.instructions: Check @connorbritain/mssql-mcp-core version and whether the documented exposure conditions apply.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade core and server to 0.6.0, reader and writer to 0.5.0. Migrate free-form whereClause inputs to structured filters; this is a breaking interface change.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed component uses the patched release and test the affected workflow with harmless inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
